title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infty}, free profinite on two generators. It is embedded in an extended group pi~ = pi^ x| S_3, the orbifold group of the quotient by the anharmonic S_3. In that group rho is the order-3 rotation (0 -> 1 -> infty) and sigma_infty is the involution fixing infty. epsilon_0 = sigma_infty rho is a 'half-loop' with epsilon_0^2 = l_0, and l_0, l_1, l_infty are the loops around the punctures.

The object studied is an automorphism u of the extended group that preserves pi^ and the inertia structure. Write u(sigma_infty) = h sigma_infty and u(rho) = g rho, with g, h in pi^. Equations (2) of the earlier pages are the torsion conditions:
- 'equation en h': (h sigma_infty)^2 = 1, i.e. h sigma_infty(h) = 1;
- 'equation en g': (g rho)^3 = 1, i.e. g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1.
The inertia condition (8 bis) says int(f) u(epsilon_0) = epsilon_0^mu, with mu in Z^ (the 'lambda' of GT). The previous page expands the left side and puts mu - 1 = 2 nu.

This page.
- Boxed 'relation des lacets' (11): sigma_infty(h) g = sigma_infty(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f).
- Grothendieck states that (g, h) determines (f, nu) and conversely that (f, nu) and one of g, h determines the other. A marginal correction notes that f is determined only modulo L_0 = <l_0>, i.e. f -> l_0^n f. This holds because l_0 = epsilon_0^2 commutes with epsilon_0.
- (12) gives the effect of composing u with int(gamma): g' = gamma g rho(gamma)^{-1}, h' = gamma h sigma_infty(gamma)^{-1}, f' = f gamma^{-1}. In other words, (g, h) behave as nonabelian 1-cocycles of Z/3 and Z/2, and f as a torsor coordinate.
- (13)-(14) solve the cocycle equations parametrically: h = beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1} with beta in pi^, and g = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} with alpha in pi^.{1, tau_infty}.

Modern reading of (13)-(14):
- h sigma_infty is an involution over sigma_infty in the virtually free profinite group pi^ x| Z/2. Finite subgroups of such groups are conjugate to the stabilisers of the orbifold points (cf. Herfort-Ribes type results). There is a single order-2 orbifold point over sigma_infty, so the conjugator beta lies in pi^.
- For rho there are two order-3 orbifold points, the fixed points e^{+-i pi/3}, which tau_infty exchanges. So g rho is conjugate to rho either by an element of pi^ or by an element of pi^ tau_infty.
- Uniqueness follows because the centralizer of rho in pi^ is trivial.

Next page. Substituting gives a single equation (15) in (alpha, beta, f, nu). Grothendieck observes that alpha lies in pi^ iff nu = 0 mod 3, i.e. mu = 1 mod 3. Geometrically, the Galois action fixes or swaps the two Q(sqrt(-3))-rational order-3 points according to the cyclotomic character mod 3. He then normalises h' = 1 by replacing u with int(beta^{-1}) u.

Purpose. This is Grothendieck's own derivation of what is now the defining system of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group (Drinfeld 1990; Ihara). His (mu, f) is GT's (lambda, f) with lambda = 2m+1, nu = m. The 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations are recast as torsion/conjugacy conditions in the S_3-extended orbifold group, and the 'loop equation' (11) couples them.
errors: In 'pour u correspondant à f, g, h, f' the list should read nu, g, h, f (f is repeated); a slip.
The main text first claims (g, h) determine f 'de manière unique'. Grothendieck himself corrects this in the margin: f is only determined modulo L_0 = <l_0>.
On the next page, (15) writes h^nu where l_1^nu (as in (11)) is meant; probably a transcription or handwriting issue.

The bare claim 'se résolvent paramétriquement de façon unique' needs two nontrivial inputs: (i) conjugacy of torsion in profinite virtually-free orbifold groups, and (ii) triviality of the centralizer of rho (resp. sigma_infty) in pi^. Neither is justified on the page; both are true but non-trivial in the profinite setting.

ideas.what: 'Relation des lacets' (11): sigma_infty(h) g = sigma_infty(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f), linking the order-2 and order-3 cocycles of an automorphism of the S_3-extended profinite pi_1 of P^1 - 3 points via the inertia-normalising element f and exponent nu, with mu = 2nu + 1.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations (2-cycle/3-cycle relations) of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT^, with lambda = 2m+1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990-91); orbifold/S_3 formulations by Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura-Schneps, Harbater-Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces the Teichmüller tower and its first two levels but does not give these equations explicitly; La Longue Marche (1981) is partly circulated, contents of this part unsure

ideas.what: Transformation rule (12) under inner automorphisms: g, h change as nonabelian 1-cocycles (twisted conjugation), f by right translation.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian group cohomology H^1(Z/n, pi^) / twisted conjugacy

ideas.what: Parametrisation of solutions of h sigma_infty(h) = 1 and g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1 as coboundaries beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}, alpha rho(alpha)^{-1}, with alpha possibly needing the extra tau_infty, i.e. torsion of the orbifold group is conjugate to the stabilisers of the orbifold points, two of which have order 3.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy of finite subgroups in profinite virtually free / orbifold fundamental groups; triviality of H^1 relative to the decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort-Ribes, Zalesskii (profinite torsion conjugacy); used in GT context by Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura

ideas.what: f is defined only modulo the centralizer <l_0> of the inertia at 0.
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation f in the commutator subgroup in GT

missed.claim: An independent, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the GT system, written as a single twisted 'loop equation' in the S_3-extended orbifold group. The 2- and 3-cycle conditions appear as torsion conditions solved by conjugators alpha, beta, together with the remark (next page) that alpha lies in pi^ iff mu = 1 mod 3.
missed.quote: Cette relation, qui relie h et g via f, peut à juste titre s'appeler la "relation des lacets".
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority material for GT, and the (alpha, beta) conjugator parametrisation is a slightly different coordinate system from the usual (lambda, f). However, the GT relations themselves are classical. Lochak-Schneps and Nakamura-Schneps used S_3/orbifold torsion formulations, and Schneps has worked on these archives, so novelty to specialists is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, essentially correct derivation of the GT-defining relations in an orbifold/S_3 form, with a careful parametrisation via conjugators of torsion elements. It is historically valuable as evidence that Grothendieck had these equations, plausibly before Drinfeld's 1990 paper. But the mathematics is now standard GT theory and the orbifold viewpoint appears in the 1990s literature, so a specialist would not be very surprised.
transcription_corrections: 'détermine f et mu de manière unique f et nu' — mu is struck; read: 'la connaissance de h et g détermine de manière unique f et nu'.
Margin note: 'f déterminé mod L_0 seulement, f -> l_0^n f (n in Z^)' — the transcription's [?] can be dropped.
In 'pour u correspondant à f, g, h, f' the first entry is likely nu (or mu), written over.
The second margin note seems to say 'Cela vaut pour gamma in pi~^ ! même pour gamma in ...'; the duplicated widetilde in the transcription is unreliable.
(14): alpha in pi~_{0,3}^ = pi^_{0,3}.{1, tau_infty} (tilde, not hat over the whole group).
